scores.reason: Random C-peptide with concurrent glucose is recommended in a specific population (insulin-treated adults with uncertain type) in the ADA/EASD 2021 consensus and reproduced in ADA Standards of Care 2026 section 2 (Figure 2.1), with stated cut-offs and validity limits. It is a consensus algorithm step, not a required or label-mandated test, and islet autoantibodies come first. Measure type: C-peptide, random (non-fasting, concurrent glucose).

scores.correction: Corrected 2026-10-20 after the pilot skeptic review (U6): ADA/EASD 2021 (PMC8481000) and ADA Standards 2026 section 2 Figure 2.1 footnote 4 say 'Where a person is insulin-treated, C-peptide must be measured prior to insulin discontinuation to exclude severe insulin deficiency'. That is a required step for the decision to stop insulin; under anchor 7 (4 only when the guideline requires the test for the decision) the score is 4. U1's reason above, which says the test is not required, is wrong for that decision; for the classification decision (autoantibodies first) the test is a recommended step.

scores.reason: Situation = insulin-treated adult, type uncertain, more than 3 years from diagnosis, where the Holt algorithm calls for C-peptide. CDC: 1.8 million US adults with type 1 and 28.8 million with diagnosed diabetes; the count of insulin-treated adults with uncertain type is not published, so the estimate is an assumption-based chain (insulin-treated adults of several million x 2-10 percent uncertain x roughly one in three needing a test in a year). Point estimate about 120,000 per year, range 30,000 to 400,000. The range spans bins 3 and 4 and the point sits near the 100,000 boundary, so low confidence. Measure type: C-peptide.

scores.reason: No guideline names an insulin (or C-peptide) measurement for post-bariatric hypoglycaemia. ADA Standards 2026 rec 8.26 says clinical evaluation should exclude other disorders and recommends CGM, with no assay named; PES 2015 (paediatric) says postprandial hypoglycaemia after fundoplication or gastric bypass shows exaggerated insulin responses detectable on oral glucose or mixed-meal tests (description, not a recommendation). Insulin at documented hypoglycaemia is part of the general adult hypoglycaemia work-up (Endocrine Society 2009, abstract only here). Scored 2 (option) rather than 1 because measurement is part of accepted evaluation text but not specific to this situation. Measure type: fasting-independent insulin (+/- C-peptide) at symptomatic nadir or after mixed meal.

scores.reason: Situation = a post-bariatric patient with suspected hypoglycaemia needing biochemical work-up. ASMBS 2023: about 157,000 sleeve and 63,000 gastric bypass procedures per year. Using the systematic review's Level A rates for needing medical attention (5 percent sleeve, 12 percent bypass) gives about 15,000 new cases per year; the same review models about 160,000 US patients needing medical management at any time. Annual patients in whom the work-up question arises: point about 30,000 (new cases plus a share of the prevalent pool), range 8,000 to 160,000. The range spans bins 3 and 4, so low confidence. Measure type: unspecified insulin at nadir or mixed-meal.

scores.reason: Both guidelines endorse pioglitazone after stroke or TIA in people with insulin resistance and prediabetes, but neither names a test, assay or threshold. ADA Standards 2026 rec 3.13 (evidence grade A, C) says pioglitazone 'may be considered' and the text describes IRIS HOMA-IR 3.0 or more; AACE 2022 rec 9.4 says it 'should be considered' in insulin resistance, prediabetes or T2D with prior TIA or stroke. The recommendation is for a drug in a defined group; measurement of insulin or HOMA-IR is not recommended or required. Scored 2 (option). Measure type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR).

scores.reason: Situation = adult with ischaemic stroke or TIA, no diabetes, deciding on pioglitazone. CDC: about 795,000 strokes a year (610,000 first), 87 percent ischaemic, so about 690,000; at least 240,000 TIAs a year (AHA statement as cited by a news page). Roughly 70 percent without diabetes (assumption) gives about 650,000; HOMA-IR above 3.0 in about 25 to 50 percent (assumption; IRIS cut-off was the highest quartile of non-diabetic populations, median in trial 4.7); after exclusions (heart failure, sample timing) about 100,000 to 300,000. Point about 200,000, range 100,000 to 400,000, inside bin 4 (100,000 to 1,000,000) on any reading, including testing every non-diabetic stroke patient (about 650,000). Measure type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR).
sources: CDC Stroke Facts, cdc.gov/stroke/data-research/facts-stats (web page, 2025-07-10)

anchor_issues: D7 rows 5 and 6: the rubric defines patients per year in whom the situation arises, but for chronic conditions (post-bariatric hypoglycaemia, insulin-treated adults of uncertain type) the pool is prevalent, not incident. I counted new cases plus a share of the prevalent pool needing a test in the year, and said so; the share is an assumption.

D7 row 6: the situation could be read as all newly diagnosed adults (about 1 million a year, bin 5) or only insulin-treated adults of uncertain type more than 3 years from diagnosis (the Holt/ADA indication). I chose the narrower reading because the guideline restricts C-peptide to that group.

D3 row 13: guidelines recommend the drug in people 'with insulin resistance' without naming a measurement. The D3 anchor 3 (recommended in a specific population) arguably fits AACE 'should be considered' (Grade A), but the recommendation is about pioglitazone, not about measuring insulin. I scored 2 for the measurement.

D3 row 5: the only guideline text that touches the measurement is general adult hypoglycaemia work-up (abstract only) and a paediatric description; no PBH-specific guideline names an insulin test. Anchor 1 (not addressed) versus 2 (option) was a judgement; I chose 2.

D3 anchor 4 'required or standard' does not say whether a consensus algorithm step (row 6) counts as standard; I scored 3 because the algorithm makes autoantibodies the first test and the C-peptide conditional.
assumptions: Insulin-treated adults with uncertain diabetes type: share 2 to 10 percent and one-third tested per year are my assumptions, not sourced; the number of insulin-treated US adults was not retrieved.
About 70 percent of ischaemic stroke and TIA patients have no diabetes, and 25 to 50 percent of them have HOMA-IR above 3.0: both are assumptions (not retrieved in this unit).
Systematic review 41966914 was read at abstract level only and the abstract was truncated in retrieval; its modelled 160,000 figure is a prevalent pool, not an annual count.
ADA Standards 2026 sections 2, 3 and 8 were read as web-page text via tools/pmc_text.py (publisher does not allow XML), by passage search, not in full.
The project-file text for row 6 (11 percent reclassified) was taken from usecases-verified.md and not re-read in the Holt full text.
